about.body:
Utopet

A desktop-mascot engine re-implemented in Python + PySide6.
Fully compatible with the original Actions.xml / Behavior.xml,
supports Japanese / Chinese / English tags, and adds a settings
GUI, a custom-action editor and multi-language switching.

hint.cal_strength: CalMode strength is a percentage. 100 = the default strength; 0 = flatten the effect (always the base value); 200 = double it.
guide.title: Can't find your pet? These are the ways back
guide.text:
Utopet has no permanent window, so closing the panel makes it look gone -- it is still running in the background.

Three ways back:/n· The tray icon -- click it for the menu; it may be tucked behind the '^' overflow arrow, drag it out
· The taskbar panel -- pick "Show taskbar panel" from the tray menu
· The pet itself -- right-click it for the full menu

With no pets left the panel comes back on its own.
Note: reinstalling does not fix "can't find it" -- it overwrites your settings instead.
lbl.climb: Allow climbing windows (walk on top / climb up)
lbl.throw: Allow throwing windows (auto-pulled back into the work area)
guide.open_taskbar_settings_tip: Opens Windows Settings > Personalization > Taskbar; set the pet to visible under "Other system tray icons"

guide.e_desktop_sub: The full menu is right there on the pet itself
guide.reinstall_warning: Note: reinstalling does NOT fix "can't find it" - it just overwrites your settings.

lib.col.name: Name
hint.library: "Disable" only hides it from the pickers; the files stay and you can enable it again at any time. Use it for packs under Program Files that cannot be removed without elevation.
msg.delete_char_confirm: Delete the character "{0}"? Its images and configuration files are removed permanently.
msg.delete_char_denied: Not allowed to delete (the program usually lives under Program Files). Delete this folder manually, or run the app as administrator and try again:/n{0}
hint.idle_gather: Gathered pets are released automatically: a cursor movement dismisses them (after at least 3 seconds), and leaving the cursor still past the value above releases them too. In the original configuration the chain that follows "gather around the cursor" is closed, so older versions never let them out again -- which is why this feature shipped disabled.
hint.window_maximized: Maximised / full-screen windows take no part in window interaction: their bottom edge coincides with the screen floor, so a pet standing on the ground would endlessly trigger "crawl along the window's bottom edge". Ordinary windowed windows are unaffected.
